title: Pet peeves
note: Each entry names a behavior the owner has corrected an assistant for repeatedly, stated so a reviewer can check work against it. The [peeves skill](SKILL.md) says how to use the entries. The commit hook writes [`peeves.csv`](peeves.csv) from this file. Edit this file and do not hand-edit the CSV.

items.note: Instructions growing through rationale, excess detail, history and comments that explain readable code.
items.look_for: non-dispositive content of any kind. UI play-by-play, correction notes, soapboxing. New content not minimally woven in.
items.owner: web-tools CLAUDE.md (before adding to a doc, ask whether another document owns it)

items.note: Carefully avoid the informal voice of online writing. The best model is a statement of facts from a legal brief: short, crisp sentences, using common terms in their most basic sense.
items.look_for: a maxim or truism, such as 'Hold inferences loosely, and keep their hedges when you retell them'; a one-line closing punch; a metaphor where a literal word exists; 'it does one thing', 'is the floor', 'held to', 'carries weight', 'does the work'; 'deliberately' or 'never' used for emphasis; a thing given wants or entitlements in place of an instruction to an actor, as in 'a wake that leaves the reader nothing new gets no reply' or 'a kit that wants Alpine reactivity gets a component wrapper'

items.note: Claims a reader cannot check, unnamed subjects and pronouns whose referents the reader has to recover.
items.look_for: 'a file here', 'some cases', 'it is complicated'; 'thing', 'whatever' or 'something' in place of a noun the sentence could name, as in 'a second thing to look at' or 'whatever view is on screen'; a sentence that cannot be checked; two replies that disagree silently

items.note: Em dashes, en dashes or double hyphens used to join ideas in prose.
items.look_for: an em dash, en dash or double hyphen between clauses
items.owner: docs/QUALIFIED-WRITING.md (no em dashes); home tools/lint-conventions.py catches em dashes and double hyphens in home only

items.note: Giving ordinary or specialized terms a private meaning, or assuming the reader shares meanings drawn from unspecified context.
items.look_for: a familiar word used for a special local concept; an unexplained coined, metaphorical or insider term; a meaning imported from another discussion or file without introducing it; competing names that leave the referent unclear

items.note: Summaries that assume the reader followed the session, already understands the subject or authored pasted material.
items.look_for: a summary, assessment or reorientation that starts mid-thought, relies on earlier turns, or credits pasted text to the owner; an ordinary reply may rely on the turn it answers

items.note: Quietly taking the work in a different direction from the owner's proposal, leaving the owner to discover the departure later.
items.look_for: a change in scope, approach, output or framing that is not called out when the direction changes; explaining the departure only after the owner notices

items.note: Treating an available rationale, measurement or precedent as sufficient to dismiss the owner's challenge. A choice can have justification and still be bad. Entertain the criticism, examine the tradeoff and revise the choice when warranted.
items.look_for: a rationale or measurement offered as if it settles whether a choice is good; a challenged choice repeated without considering the criticism; weak reasons used to dismiss an idea

items.note: Asking the owner to inspect available evidence, settle a question the assistant can resolve or approve an already agreed next step.
items.look_for: 'Shall I proceed?' or 'Want me to...?' on a path already agreed; a question whose answer is in the repo

items.note: Handing the owner choices without the assessment and recommendation needed to decide.
items.look_for: a list of options without a recommendation; a question with no context to answer it
items.owner: home CLAUDE.md; the portable ask-question-guard hook refuses only the AskUserQuestion tool, not a menu written in prose

items.note: References without usable links, render links that miss the changed view and links that stop short of the named item.
items.look_for: a viewable change with no render link; a link that loads blank or lands on the wrong view; a standalone page link where the app route renders it (framed pages excepted, per home CLAUDE.md)
items.owner: docs/CONVERSATION.md (npm run showing picks the link)

items.note: Reporting an inferred result as demonstrated, handing over an unexamined screenshot or proposing a fix before checking the cause.
items.look_for: 'should work'; a screenshot sent without comment on what it shows; asking the owner to run the test

items.text: Three options for a visual choice
items.note: For an open visual choice, show about three options as screenshots and recommend one.
items.look_for: a single guess, or options described in words

items.note: Adding a mechanism, category or separate interface when an existing one serves the job. One-off interfaces bypass the app shell, file viewer or shared component without a reason the existing interface cannot serve.
items.look_for: a new folder, registry, name or layer next to one that already exists; a workaround mechanism for a simple problem

items.note: When cleaning up, reduce rather than add; do not add rules, guards or documentation for a single incident or a hypothetical, and do not widen the scope (orchestration, fan-outs) without being asked.
items.look_for: a guard script for one mistake; a fan-out nobody asked for; a cleanup that added lines
items.owner: web-tools CLAUDE.md (wary of improvements for hypothetical problems)

items.note: Before acting or asserting what exists, read the relevant skill or style guide and check the latest main, other repos and open branches.
items.look_for: a page built without html-style; 'there is no X' from a stale or shallow clone

items.note: Handoff prompts that prescribe detailed steps, solutions or option rankings beyond the goal and necessary context.
items.look_for: a step-by-step handoff where an outcome and constraints would suffice; instructions that leave the receiving session little room to exercise judgment

items.note: Leaving feasible work for another session, stopping before an authorized merge or declaring a tool failure after trying one route.
items.look_for: stopping at 'ready for your review' after being told to merge; a PR left with a conflict

items.note: Timed check-ins and redundant status messages about unchanged PR or CI state. A new failure, review or merge can warrant a message.
items.look_for: a scheduled CI check-in; the same status repeated after each event; redundant PR or CI status messages when the state has not changed
items.owner: docs/CONVERSATION.md (PR events); the portable send-later guard refuses only send_later

items.note: Pages spending space explaining their purpose or controls when the structure and labels could make the purpose clear.
items.look_for: a sentence on the page saying what the page or a section is for

items.note: Repeated headings and controls, unnecessary boxes and padding, or an artificially narrow reading column. Comfortable text size and contrast remain requirements.
items.look_for: generous padding, a card inside a card, a rounded box inside a full-bleed viewer; small or pale text bought for compactness

items.note: Make every view work at phone width: no sideways page scroll, tables scroll inside their container under sticky headers, controls neither wrap nor shift, inputs at 16px.
items.look_for: horizontal page overflow at 390px; a control row that wraps; layout that moves when a count gains a digit
items.owner: web-tools page-measures (npm run shot --measure) reports sideways overflow only; the rest is a reader's check

items.note: Tiles that put a label over a big number without the comparison, baseline or movement needed to interpret the figure.
items.look_for: stats, stat-value, a KPI grid

items.note: Labels that spend several words on an action a plain word or recognizable icon could express.
items.look_for: 'Open the guide', 'Copy to stage'; a book icon followed by the word Read

items.note: Dark tooltips and overlays, heavy outlines and saturated controls. Tooltips use the app components and remain brief, light and dismissible on touch.
items.look_for: black fills or pills, outlined buttons inside an outlined card, dark text on saturated red

items.note: Accordions and nesting that hide list structure or interrupt reading. The list and separate detail panel used for Peeves is the preferred example.
items.look_for: sections stacked down the page; collapse and expand used to hide structure

items.note: Opaque identifiers used as labels, export dates or internal state shown without a reader purpose, and warnings for ordinary conditions.
items.look_for: a hash or id shown as a label; 'you' in page copy; a warning for an expected state

items.note: Interactions respond at once and can be undone: no hover delay or long animation, tooltips dismiss, there is a way to back out, destructive clicks confirm or undo.
items.look_for: a delay before highlight; a click that deletes with no undo

items.note: Give a first draft craft: study the app's best existing views before designing, and never ship a stock template.
items.look_for: a generic prototype layout; the dashboard template's tiles and hero

items.note: Align icons, pins and highlights with the line of text beside them, and check it in a screenshot.
items.look_for: an icon sitting a pixel or two high or low against its label

items.note: Information embedded in presentation or scripts, a Markdown table parsed to recover structured rows, or stored values already available from git or the app.
items.look_for: values typed into HTML or Python; a script that parses Markdown into a table; a stored date git already has

items.note: Source paragraphs broken across lines at an arbitrary width. Paragraphs remain continuous; the renderer controls visual wrapping.
items.look_for: a paragraph broken across lines at a fixed width in a .md file or a PR body

items.note: Emphasizing distinctions of unclear relevance, or shadow-boxing with implausible suppositions. Watch for any blanket negation: the word "nothing" is often a flag that the preceding statement leaves some conspicuous gap that the term then tries to paper over. Close the gap, and avoid the patch.
items.look_for: 'draws no underline', 'adds no claim', 'names no file', 'open no new ones', 'nothing opens it', 'leaves the reader nothing new', 'there is nothing to act on'; repeated 'not X, but Y' contrasts; rejecting an alternative the reader never raised

items.note: Aliases and fallbacks kept without a named dependency that requires them. An outside caller can justify compatibility. A migration names the concrete completion step that allows the old form to be removed.
items.look_for: 'still resolves' or 'keeps a saved link working' with no outside reference found; an alias or legacy fallback whose consumers are all in the estate; a removal date with no completion step

items.note: Calling a list a ledger, census, catalog or similar term and expecting the word to establish the list's meaning. The defined uses of registry and stream retain their existing exceptions.
items.look_for: the news ledger, a skills catalog, the census test, a branch survey; a list term implying that a list is complete, append-only or authoritative without saying so
items.owner: docs/registries.md (registries and streams); home CLAUDE.md (name the subject, not the genre)

items.note: Avoid modal dialogs; consider a panel-tip, the Swipe Deck takeover, or another more fluid alternative.
items.look_for: showModal(), modal-box, a dimmed backdrop

items.note: A sentence that turns on "so", presenting one cause as forcing one result.
items.look_for: 'checks passed, so there's nothing to act on'; 'the data keys stay, so no markup or coding changes'; 'that is the prose the house style rules out, so it should go'; ', so a reader can stop there'

items.note: Edits that weaken guidance that exists to steer away from model intuition. The problem can involve removing pointed language or softening it with material that emphasizes conventional rationales that the guidance intends to de-emphasize.
items.look_for: a line that steers against model intuition, cut or reworded into a general statement, such as 'especially use of 🟢 where direction has already been set' dropped from a policy urging the assistant to proceed; a caveat, exception or conventional rationale added beside such a line that restores the intuition, such as 'acting on it waits for the owner's word'

items.note: Direction with an unclear standard and weak support. Broad guidance can be useful when surrounded by more detailed considerations. Otherwise, a directive that points the reader back to their own judgment is typically better left unsaid.
items.look_for: directive language, often not to take some action, based on subjective judgment; a last sentence of a paragraph punctuating an idea without adding clarity

items.text: Domain page links to GitHub, chats
items.note: A page of a domain app, an app such as budget-drs's whose subject is a field of work, linking to or referencing GitHub or a chat. This peeve does not concern the Web Tools app, which focuses on interaction with GitHub and AI.
items.look_for: a link on a domain app page that opens github.com, claude.ai or chatgpt.com; a figure's source given as a chat

items.note: Long, undifferentiated paragraphs in documents or replies that pack several subjects into one block of prose instead of giving distinct topics, mechanisms or steps separate paragraphs or tables.
items.look_for: one long paragraph covering several subjects (such as architecture, clone reads and build outputs in one block); a reply or README passage that shifts topic without a paragraph break

items.note: A sentence that won’t end. Find bite size ideas that build into the larger point. If support is needed, add it after the period. Break up complex sentences, remove excessive detail, and scrutinize for clear flow of ideas. Consider moving up a level.
items.look_for: a second complete claim joined on with ", and", ", which", ", so" or ", because"; a clause opening on an -ing verb tacked onto the end; conditions stacked before the main clause; a qualifier added to answer a reviewer's question, as in 'When a view's `data-find-input` element also carries `data-find-submit`, naming a method of the view, the find pill's bar shows a Results button, and Enter or that button passes the text typed in the bar to the method.'; a short sentence that names many things and describes code where the effect would do, as in 'Enter or the Results button calls the named method with the bar's text.'

items.text: Fix the sentence, add no note
items.note: Correct a living document by fixing the sentence: the smallest edit that removes the error, with no new paragraph and no 'formerly', 'corrected' or 'superseded' note.
items.look_for: an error fix that grows the file; a sentence recording what the text used to say
items.owner: home CLAUDE.md (status markers retired: fix the sentence)

items.note: Familiarity with a local or specialized term being assumed of the reader. An established technical term can still need an introduction.
items.look_for: a coinage or insider term (pin, hunk, emitter, the estate, guide delimiter) used without a definition

items.note: Introduce the subject before referring to it, and name the referent each time: no bare 'this', 'it', 'that one file'; each bullet must stand alone.
items.look_for: a pronoun or definite phrase whose referent is several sentences back; a bullet that only makes sense after the one before

items.note: Say a thing once: one owner per statement, linked from elsewhere, never restated in a second file, a header and its list, or a table and its caption.
items.look_for: the same claim in two documents, or in a heading and the line under it

items.note: Do not use the words the owner has retired: register in a coined sense, carry as a verb for what a file holds, carrier for a data file, and tray.
items.look_for: a guidance register, a file that carries a list, a data carrier, a tray of material

items.note: Give one thing one name everywhere: file name, label and title match, with no aliases, exception tables or number suffixes.
items.look_for: a file called one thing and labelled another; 'v2', 'new', or a second name for an old concept

items.note: Name things for what they are, not by metaphor or vague umbrella.
items.look_for: a figurative label (rack, a spicy name) or a catch-all group label (authored) where a plain descriptive one exists

items.note: Link every file, folder, PR, session or page you mention; in a directory listing or index, link each entry to the file that resolves what that entry is.
items.look_for: a path, folder entry or PR number in prose without a link; a directory bullet that names a folder with no link to the folder's README, page or script

items.note: Separate what was demonstrated from what was inferred from reading code, and hedge unverified claims; do not call an assessment completed work.
items.look_for: 'works' for something only read; 'all' or 'every' without having checked

items.note: Resolve open questions wherever the evidence allows; do not hand the owner new items to review.
items.look_for: an open-questions list that grew; items the session could have settled

items.note: Show proposed wording for a doc or skill as a diff in chat, with context and a link to the file, before committing it.
items.look_for: a doc or skill edit committed without the owner seeing the wording
items.owner: web-tools .githooks/commit-msg via skills/hooks/commit-consent.py (modified Markdown only); skills/hooks/warn-governing-docs.sh at edit time

items.note: Finish what can be finished in this session; do not defer it to a later session, a follow-up, or someone else.
items.look_for: 'left for a follow-up', 'out of scope', 'not mine to land' for work the session could do

items.note: Do not file a tracker task unless the owner asks for one.
items.look_for: a new task file the owner did not endorse

items.note: Do not propose deleting a feature, page or branch unless its removal was clearly intended.
items.look_for: a cleanup that removes working features

items.note: When a tool or PR route fails, try another route before reporting it blocked.
items.look_for: 'could not create the PR' after one failed call

items.note: Remove what repeats or carries no use: a header that restates the tab, count badges on tabs, duplicate buttons, filters and pills nobody needs.
items.look_for: a heading echoing the selected tab; a count on every tab; two controls for one action

items.note: Reuse the app's components and conventions (viewer, swipe deck, tooltip kits, toggles, tabs), and show content in the app's own viewer, keeping the GitHub link a view carries.
items.look_for: a one-off control where a kit exists; a link out where the viewer could show the file
items.owner: skills/html-style/SKILL.md; docs/APP.md (every new view carries its GitHub link)

items.note: Use the full width; never narrow text to a reading column or a centered corridor.
items.look_for: max-w-prose, max-w-2xl to 4xl, container mx-auto, a ch cap
items.owner: skills/html-style/SKILL.md (rule 3); the reading-column hook refuses class caps at edit time, and misses caps in CSS or written through the shell

items.note: Tooltips: never a fact in a title attribute, and never a daisyUI tooltip, data-tip or question-mark cursor; use the title-tip or panel-tip kit, a few words, light, closing on tap.
items.look_for: title=, data-tip, cursor-help, a dark tooltip, a tooltip paragraph
items.owner: skills/html-style/SKILL.md (rule 10); npm run stranded-titles lists facts parked in a title, advisory

items.note: Show new views inside the app shell at their route, and put findings in data the app displays, not in a standalone page or a Markdown report.
items.look_for: a standalone HTML page for something that belongs in a view; findings left only in a .md file

items.note: Keep code comments short and few.
items.look_for: long comment blocks explaining code that reads plainly

items.note: A link lands on the specific item it names, and its text says what that item is.
items.look_for: a link that opens a tab or a document top instead of the item; the same generic link text repeated; a link whose text does not name its target
